description.text:
The promos of Japan's Platinum years: 51 cards, 001/DPt-P to 051/DPt-P, released from October 2008 to August 2009. The run began alongside Galactic's Conquest, the first expansion of the DPt series, when DP-P gave way to DPt-P.

Many were prizes: at Gym Challenge store tournaments, at Challenge Hiroba, at the tournaments held for the release of each new expansion, in the Pokémon Battle Tour 2009 and at the tournament that chose Japan's World Championships players. Others came from release campaigns and Special Packs for Galactic's Conquest and the sets after it, the Pokémon Daisuki Club's member ranks, the film Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime and its Movie Commemoration Special Pack, an official Arceus deck case and Weekly Shōnen Sunday.

description.text:
The third Pokémon Center 10th anniversary card. To mark ten years since the Pokémon Centers opened, all five stores, Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka and Yokohama, gave it to each shopper from 14 to 28 November 2008, one per person while stocks lasted. Squirtle was picked by a vote over Meowth. Like the earlier cards' Shopping and Little Errand, its attack Souvenir Pick (おみやげえらび) brings a card from the deck: it looks at the top two and keeps one.

Pikachu came first, from 30 May 2008, in a slightly different version at each store (098 to 102/DP-P), then Charmander 124/DP-P from 22 August 2008. Bulbasaur 030/DPt-P followed from 4 April 2009, when shoppers who brought any two different cards of the four got a Pokémon Card Game coin. Yuka Morii made it.

description.text:
The card of Lucario, the "department head" (ルカリオ部長) of Pokémon Sunday (ポケモン☆サンデー), TV Tokyo's Sunday-morning Pokémon show. From the episode of 14 December 2008, the show followed the making of the card: Lucario and Robert (ロバート) visited the people who make Pokémon card illustrations in 3D computer graphics, in clay and in 2D drawing, Robert tried drawing Lucario too, and Lucario chose Mitsuhiro Arita's 2D drawing, striking its usual "Roger!" (ラジャー) pose for it.

From 17 January 2009, while stocks lasted, shops across Japan gave the card to anyone who brought one Fighting Pokémon card to trade and said the password "Roger!", one per person, with a Bonds to the End of Time fun book. The fun book points out its secrets: a P.S.C. logo in the background, the Roger pose, the Pokémon Sunday logo, and a Poké-Body also called Roger, under which players reply to each other with a hand on the chest and a "Roger!". Its attack Brick Break (かわらわり) was chosen because Lucario broke roof tiles on the show. The card can be used in official tournaments.

description.text:
The fourth and last Pokémon Center 10th anniversary card. To mark ten years since the Pokémon Centers opened, all their stores gave it to each shopper from 4 to 17 April 2009, one per person while stocks lasted, and shoppers who also brought any two different cards of the four got a Pokémon Card Game coin. Like the earlier cards' attacks, its attack Present (プレゼント) brings a card from the deck, here any card on a coin flip.

description.text:
The trophy card of the final stage of the Pokémon World Championships Japan Representative Tournament (ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス日本代表決定大会), which chose Japan's players for the 2009 World Championships. After a first stage in all 47 prefectures from October 2008 and six regional second-stage tournaments in March and April 2009, the final stage was held at the Prince Park Tower Tokyo on 4 May 2009, for card game and video game players together.

The top finishers of both games got the card set in an acrylic plaque showing their placing, blue for the card game and red for the video game: 36 cards in all, 20 to card game players and 16 to video game players.
